title: Hongye Elementary School's 1968 little league team and Taiwan's baseball fever

sources.title: Taiwan in Time: Legend of the 'red leaf' in question (2016-08-21)
Storied Hongye team sets sights on Little League World Series berth (2026-06-23)
Baseball gives Taiwan's image a boost (2008-08-07)

facts.text: Hongye Elementary School is in Hongye Village, Yanping Township, Taitung County; its 1968 team was made up mostly of Bunun children.
According to a May 1968 news report, the school had only 114 students and five staff members.
The village was poor, and the players are said to have trained using sticks instead of bats and stones instead of balls.
In March 1968 Hongye won first place in a youth tournament in Tainan, then said it lacked the money to travel to Taipei for the national tournament.
After the media reported the team's situation, donations poured in; the team went to Taipei and won the national championship.
On August 25, 1968, Hongye beat a visiting Japanese all-star youth team 7-0 in front of a crowd of about 20,000.
Until that game, a youth team from Taiwan had never beaten one from Japan.
Excited fans threw money onto the field, and the Ministry of Education promised the school money for sports equipment.
The 1968 win is widely credited with starting Taiwan's nationwide baseball craze.
In 1969 a Taiwanese team won the Little League World Series for the first time.
In the 1970s, Taiwanese teams won seven Little League World Series championships.

Many later accounts said Hongye had beaten Wakayama, the Japanese world champion team, but a researcher noted that Wakayama was then taking part in the Little League World Series held in the United States, which ended on August 24.
In April 1969 the team's coach and manager were convicted of forging documents: five players' ages had been falsified, and players from outside the school had played under other students' names.
Hongye itself never played in the Little League World Series, and it quickly lost its fame because it had used overage players in 1968 and 1969.
Hongye Village has a little league baseball memorial hall that displays photos, baseball equipment and news clippings.
In 2026 Hongye won its first national Little League title, ending Taitung County's 20-year wait for a national Little League championship.
